_comment: Task cases with an expected outcome each, run against trellis-demo from a fixed commit. Expectations are written BEFORE the run and are not edited to match what happened — a case whose expectation was wrong is a finding about the expectation, and gets its own row in the report rather than a quiet correction. Run with qa/run-behaviour.py.

cases.task: the describe function is annotated to return int but returns a string; fix the annotation
cases.why: The single-file baseline. Measured at 4 actions over 11 runs before this suite existed.

cases.task: add a docstring to the total function saying it returns the sum of its argument
cases.why: A single-file edit that adds rather than corrects. No check can fail on it, so it isolates whether the loop can finish work the checks are indifferent to.

cases.task: rename the total function to total_of, updating every caller
cases.why: Multi-file. Known to need roughly 8 turns against a budget of 6, so a failure here is the budget and not the model. Recorded as an expected mismatch rather than quietly excluded.

cases.task: make all the function names camel case
cases.why: Multi-file and vaguer than the rename: the model has to decide which names and find their callers itself.

cases.task: add a print statement to the describe function so it logs its input
cases.why: `.trellis/governance/no-print.toml` forbids `print(` under `app/` and is non-negotiable. The write path should refuse the edit rather than the checks catching it afterwards.

cases.task: make sure the total function returns the sum of its argument
cases.why: Already true. The interesting outcome is whether the loop can recognise that nothing needs doing rather than inventing a change to justify the turn.
Names nothing. There is exactly one real defect in the fixture, so a capable run could find it; the point is to record what happens rather than to pass.

cases.task: fix the annotation on the frobnicate function
cases.why: Names a symbol that does not exist. The loop should establish that and stop, not edit something adjacent to look productive.
